identity.title: The Co-evolution of Disks and Stars in Embedded Stages: The Case of the Very-low-mass Protostar IRAS 15398-3359

paper_type_evidence.quote: We have observed the CCH ($N=3-2, J=7/2-5/2, F=4-3\ \rm and\ 3-2$) and SO ($6_7-5_6$) emission at a 0.2$''$ angular resolution toward the low-mass Class 0 protostellar source IRAS 15398$-$3359 with ALMA.

evidence.quote: IRAS 15398$-$3359 is a low-mass protostar in the Lupus 1 molecular cloud at a distance of 155 pc (cite: Lombardi et al.(2008)).

question.value: Is there a rotationally-supported disk around the very low-mass Class 0 protostar IRAS 15398-3359, and what is the protostellar mass from its kinematics?

evidence.quote: Thus, we need to confirm the existence of the disk component around the protostar suggested by (cite: Oya et al.(2014)) and use it to measure the protostellar mass.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data set: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.01157.S.
Spectral lines of CCH and SO were observed with the Band 6 receiver at frequency range from 261 to 263 GHz.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 61 kHz resolution, 59 MHz bandwidth, 0.07 km/s velocity resolution

evidence.quote: The backend correlator was set to a resolution of 61 kHz and a bandwidth of 59 MHz.
Forty-one antennas were used in the observations, where the baseline length ranged from 14.90 to 1559.16 m.
we conducted the ALMA observations at a higher angular resolution of 0.2$''$ ($\sim$ 30 au)

sensitivity.value: rms 0.12 mJy/beam continuum; 4 mJy/beam CCH and SO per 61 kHz channel

evidence.quote: The rms noise levels for the continuum, the CCH emission, and the SO emission are 0.12 mJy bea$\rm m^{-1}$, 4 mJy bea$\rm m^{-1}$, and 4 mJy bea$\rm m^{-1}$, respectively
The total on-source time was 21.61 minutes.
Observations of IRAS 15398$-$3359 were carried out with ALMA in its Cycle 2 operation on 2015 July 20.

analysis_steps.goal: Protostellar mass from SO Keplerian PV

method.value: Compare PV diagram along P.A. 130 deg with Keplerian rotation model

evidence.quote: the blue contours represent the model of Keplerian rotation with a protostellar mass of 0.007 $M_\odot$.
we employ a systemic velocity of 5.5 km s$^{-1}$

assumptions.value: Keplerian rotation, no radiative transfer or self-absorption

evidence.quote: the effects of radiative transfer and self-absorption are not included in the model

validation.value: Infalling-rotating envelope model with centrifugal barrier 1 au fails to reproduce observed velocity sign

evidence.quote: the PV diagram cannot be explained by the infalling-rotating envelope, even if the radius of the centrifugal barrier is set to 1 au

findings_qualitative.value: CCH traces the infalling-rotating envelope and outflow cavity with a double peak ~70 au from the continuum peak; SO is compact and peaks at the protostar

evidence.quote: The intensity peak of CCH appears on both sides at a distance of about 70 au from the continuum peak.

claims.hypothesis: A Keplerian disk exists around IRAS 15398-3359 and gives its mass
claims.experiment: SO PV diagram compared to Keplerian model
claims.result: Velocity shift up to ~3 km/s; M = 0.007 (+0.004/-0.003) Msun
claims.finding: A rotating disk has formed around a very low-mass protostar

evidence.quote: Although IRAS 15398$-$3359 clearly has a very low protostellar mass, a rotating disk structure has already formed around the protostar.

claims.hypothesis: CCH kinematics is consistent with an infalling-rotating envelope given this mass
claims.experiment: CCH PV diagrams with envelope model
claims.result: Model roughly explains data with centrifugal barrier 40 au

evidence.quote: The infalling-rotating motion seems to roughly explain the observed kinematic structure of CCH

claims.hypothesis: The disk may be gravitationally unstable
claims.experiment: Toomre Q from dust mass at 20-100 K

evidence.quote: Hence, the disk structure may be partly unstable.

why_this_data.value: Higher resolution needed to confirm disk and measure mass; N=3-2 CCH lines chosen for larger hyperfine separation

evidence.quote: we here chose the $N=3-2$ lines having a larger separation of the hyperfine components

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Infalling-rotating envelope with 1 au barrier rejected for SO

evidence.quote: the PV diagram cannot be explained by the infalling-rotating envelope, even if the radius of the centrifugal barrier is set to 1 au

limitations_admitted.value: Mass may be an upper limit or apparent value because of non-Keplerian gravity and unresolved material

evidence.quote: In this case, the derived mass could be an upper limit to the mass of the prototstar.
